newsitem.title: USA: Universal Standard seeks oper cost cuts.
newsitem.headline: Universal Standard seeks oper cost cuts.

text.p: Universal Standard Medical Laboratories Inc said Wednesday it could cut up to $9 million in annual operating costs by the end of 1997.

"Projects implemented in the second and third quarters are expected to eliminate approximately $4 million of annual operating costs and we continue on track with additional projects for implementation through the end of 1997 which could eliminate up to an additional $5 million of operating costs," said Chip Jennings, chief executive officer.
Earlier Wednesday, the clinical medical laboratory reported a third quarter net loss of $688,000, or $0.10 a share, compared to $979,000, or $0.15 a share a year ago.
Managed care revenue in the quarter fell to $4.2 million from $4.8 million a year ago, due to a program that expired during the summer months and was renewed at a reduced level, the company said.
Fee-for-service revenue fell to $9.4 million from $11.9 million, primarily due to a 15 percent decline in patient visits, the company said.
Universal Standard shares were unchanged at 2-3/8 Wednesday.
